topic: Ship It Right 03/04: Your UI isn't the problem

cover.headline: Your UI Isn’t the Problem
cover.subtitle: Make your app feel fast, clear, and usable.

slides.title: Image Compression
slides.tip: Resize images to their display dimensions and use modern formats such as WebP or AVIF when supported.
slides.quote: Large images can make a polished app feel slow before users even reach the good part.

slides.title: Page Load Speed Check
slides.tip: Measure real loading performance, test on mobile and slower networks, and prioritize the biggest bottlenecks.
slides.quote: A slow app costs users time, patience, and sometimes the next click.

slides.title: Color Contrast Fixes
slides.tip: Check text, buttons, and links for sufficient contrast, and don’t use color as the only way to communicate meaning.
slides.quote: Good design is readable design. Don’t make users guess what the text says.

slides.title: Mobile Responsiveness
slides.tip: Test real layouts, navigation, forms, and tap targets on narrow screens and actual devices.
slides.quote: Your app should remain usable across screen sizes, not merely shrink to fit them.

slides.title: Lazy Loading
slides.tip: Lazy-load below-the-fold content where appropriate, but don’t lazy-load the main image or content needed for the initial view.
slides.quote: Load non-critical images and heavy components only when they’re needed.

slides.title: Optimize Assets
slides.tip: Remove unused assets, compress files, split code where useful, and avoid shipping large dependencies without a reason.
slides.quote: Every unnecessary byte makes the browser do work your users never asked for.

slides.title: Recap
slides.description: Save this checklist for your next UI review.

caption.caption:
Your UI isn’t the problem. How it loads, reads and behaves on a phone usually is.

Six checks to make your app feel fast, clear and usable.
